s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral weakness and vomiting with a history of transient neurological symptoms
salient_findings: Right ankle clonus and upgoing plantar response
key_facts: 36-year-old man of Indian origin
Presented at 2:30 a.m. with acute symptoms
Awoke around midnight with headache and vomiting
No visual change or speech disturbance
History of odd sensations and occasional tremors in right arm and leg
No medical history
Nonsmoker, denied alcohol or drug use
Normal vital signs
Normal cardiorespiratory examination
Incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in left parasagittal frontal cortex on CT
Normal CT angiography and CT perfusion
Normal laboratory studies except for total protein of 87 g/L
Normal chest radiograph, ECG, and transthoracic echocardiography
Recent ischemic infarction in left paramedian medulla on MRI

raw.rationale: The patient presented with acute right-sided weakness and vomiting, and brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla, which is consistent with an ischemic stroke.

rejected.label: Cavernous malformation
rejected.why: Although a small frontal cavernoma was noted on CT and MRI, it is not directly related to the patient's acute symptoms and is considered an incidental finding.

rejected.label: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome
rejected.why: There is no evidence of vasoconstriction on CT angiography or MR angiography, and the patient's symptoms do not fit the typical presentation of this condition.

rejected.label: Central nervous system vasculitis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of inflammation or vasculitis on laboratory studies or imaging, and the patient's symptoms do not fit the typical presentation of this condition.

rejected.label: Moyamoya disease
rejected.why: There is no evidence of moyamoya disease on CT angiography or MR angiography, and the patient's symptoms do not fit the typical presentation of this condition.
